gen-gf-itim-general-sans: Casual hand-written letters give Itim a friendly, jotted look, with only a short climb to the ascenders. But General Sans fills each line with smooth, steady strokes, and it reads best when text stays brief.
gen-gf-itim-satoshi: Itim writes in casual, friendly strokes that look jotted down quickly, rising only a short way to the ascenders. And Satoshi, with soaring lowercase and uniformly cut strokes, is happiest holding a couple of lines.
gen-gf-itim-switzer: Friendly Itim looks jotted by hand, with a short climb to its ascenders. Switzer draws wire-like, tubular letters with c tips held well apart, so it wants brevity, not endless paragraphs.
gen-gf-itim-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips well apart and its diagonals as hefty as its stems. Work Sans handles the modern, dependable work, while Itim does best at casual handwritten charm in brief bursts.
gen-gf-jaini-purva-fs-paquito: Expressive and bold, Jaini Purva locks glyphs together like keyed puzzle pieces, with a tiny step to lowercase. And Paquito, a confident serif whose caps hug its lowercase, is better when text stays short.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-archivo: Jim Nightshade packs its handwritten letters so close they blur into a dark, relaxed texture. But Archivo throws its curves open outward beneath a commanding x-height, best for just a few lines.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-fs-asap: Asap is readable, with c forms like open arcs and lowercase nearly matching the capitals. Asap leaves the showy work to Jim Nightshade, whose dark scrawl belongs in oversized words and brief lines.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-fs-epilogue: Epilogue is approachable, with a wire-like monoline skeleton, curvy unclamped letters and stubby ascender tips on a tall-bodied lowercase. Jim Nightshade's dark, close-set scrawl belongs in oversized words and quick lines.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-fs-supreme: Supreme looks crisp, a heavy-looking band of text through the middle. Jim Nightshade's marker-tip scrawl brings the relaxed mood, while Supreme's held-open curves rein it in for a quick read.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-manrope: Letters packed close enough to blur into a dark texture mark Jim Nightshade, while Manrope keeps a bright gap at every curve. Fine for a note, but a long essay would wear thin fast.
